(2025), and Fed. R. App. P. 15(a), Exelon Corporation' hereby petitions this Court

for review of the following order and notice of the Federal Energy Regulatory

       On November 22, 2024, Constellation Energy Generation, LLC filed a

complaint at FERC in FERC Docket No. EL25-20, against PJM Interconnection,

L.L.C. which operates transmission facilities owned by Exelon. On February 20,

2025, FERC initiated its own investigation, naming numerous entities as

respondents including the transmission-owning affiliates of Exelon, and

consolidating that new proceeding with the EL25-20 complaint. PJM

Interconnection, L.L.C. et al.; Order Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the

Federal Power Act and Consolidating with Other Proceedings, 190 FERC ¶ 61,115

(February 20, 2025). On December 18, 2025, FERC issued its ruling on the

complaint proceedings, requiring various modifications to the rates and terms of

transmission service provided by Exelon. December 18, 2025 Order, Attachment

A. Exelon timely sought rehearing on January 16, 2026, in the proceeding below.

Under the Federal Power Act, "[u]nless the Commission acts upon [an] application

for rehearing within thirty days after it is filed, such application may be deemed to

have been denied." 16 U.S.C. § 8251(a). Here, the Exelon application for rehearing

may be deemed denied because FERC failed to act upon it within 30 days

(February 17, 2026). On February 20, 2026, FERC issued a Notice of Denial of

Rehearing By Operation of Law. Because Exelon is aggrieved by FERC's action,

                B.      Behind the Meter Generation

        retail BTMG),19 the Tariff allows load serving entities (LSEs) that provide service to

        calculation of their peak demand for the purpose of determining NITS charges.2° The
        Commission has previously found that BTMG netting is just and reasonable because it
        would encourage load response during periods when generation or transmission are in
        short supply and prices are rising.2I The Commission has also found that "charges for
        use of PJM's transmission system should be allocated to network customers based on a
        network customer's actual use of PJM's system, consistent with the principle of cost
        causation."22
